name: Serverless Data Lake on AWS
description: Design an automatically configured, event-driven serverless data lake on AWS for ingesting, storing, processing, and analyzing data with proper governance.
user_problem: Design a serverless data lake on AWS with the following requirements: (1) Automated data ingestion from multiple sources with event-driven processing, (2) Scalable and cost-effective storage with tiered lifecycle policies, (3) Serverless ETL processing for data transformation and cataloging, (4) Interactive SQL query capability for ad-hoc analysis, (5) Data governance with fine-grained access control and a data catalog, (6) Workflow orchestration for multi-step data processing pipelines, (7) Monitoring, auditing, and proper security across all components.

reference_architecture.full_text:
This architecture demonstrates how to build an automatically configured data lake on AWS using an event-driven, serverless, and scalable architecture. It leverages AWS managed services to ingest, store, process, and analyze data, offering a secure, flexible, and cost-effective design with proper data governance. This approach provides greater agility, flexibility, and reliability compared to traditional data management systems. The entire solution is built as a codified application using infrastructure-as-code (IaC) and a continuous integration, continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipeline.

Data Storage Layer: Amazon S3 serves as the central data lake storage, providing virtually unlimited, highly durable (99.999999999% durability), and scalable object storage. Data is organized into multiple zones within S3 buckets following a medallion architecture: a raw zone for ingested source data in its original format, a processed zone for cleaned and transformed data, and a curated zone for business-ready, aggregated datasets optimized for analytics. S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves objects between access tiers based on changing access patterns, reducing storage costs by up to 40%. S3 Lifecycle policies transition infrequently accessed data to S3 Glacier for long-term archival at significantly reduced cost. S3 Object Lock provides write-once-read-many (WORM) protection for regulatory compliance. Server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys protects data at rest, and S3 bucket policies enforce access control in conjunction with AWS Lake Formation permissions. S3 Event Notifications trigger downstream processing when new objects land in the raw zone.

Data Ingestion Layer: Amazon EventBridge acts as the central serverless event bus that triggers data processing workflows in response to data arrival events, enabling fully automated pipelines. EventBridge supports over 100 built-in event sources from AWS services and SaaS integrations. EventBridge rules filter events using content-based patterns, routing specific event types to the appropriate downstream targets such as Lambda functions, Step Functions state machines, or SQS queues. Amazon SQS provides reliable message queuing to decouple data ingestion from processing, ensuring no data loss during high-volume ingestion bursts. SQS supports both standard queues for maximum throughput and FIFO queues for exactly-once, ordered processing. Dead-letter queues (DLQs) capture messages that fail processing after configurable retry attempts, preventing data loss and enabling investigation of failures. AWS Lambda functions handle lightweight event-driven processing tasks such as data validation, file format detection, schema validation, metadata extraction, triggering workflows, and sending notifications. Lambda automatically scales to handle thousands of concurrent data files arriving simultaneously.

Data Processing and ETL Layer: AWS Glue provides serverless ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) capabilities for large-scale data transformation. Glue jobs run on a managed Apache Spark environment, automatically provisioning and scaling the compute resources needed for each job. Glue supports both Python (PySpark) and Scala for ETL script development. AWS Glue Crawlers automatically discover and catalog data schemas by scanning data in S3, populating the AWS Glue Data Catalog with table definitions, column types, and partition information. The AWS Glue Data Catalog serves as a centralized, persistent metadata repository compatible with Apache Hive Metastore, making data across the lake discoverable and queryable by multiple analytics services. Glue Data Quality validates data against user-defined rules during ETL jobs, flagging or quarantining records that fail quality checks. AWS Step Functions orchestrates multi-step data processing workflows, coordinating Lambda functions, Glue jobs, and other AWS services in a visual, JSON-defined state machine. Step Functions provides built-in error handling with retry and catch blocks, parallel processing branches, choice states for conditional logic, and wait states for human approval workflows. Step Functions Express Workflows handle high-volume, short-duration data processing tasks at reduced cost.

Analytics and Query Layer: Amazon Athena enables interactive SQL queries directly against data stored in S3 using the Glue Data Catalog for schema definitions, with no servers or clusters to manage. Athena uses Presto and Apache Spark engines and supports standard SQL including complex joins, window functions, and nested data queries. Athena charges only for the amount of data scanned per query, and costs can be reduced by up to 90% by using columnar formats like Apache Parquet or ORC with data partitioning and compression. Athena federated queries can also query data in Amazon Redshift, Amazon DynamoDB, Amazon RDS, and other data sources through Lambda-based connectors. Amazon QuickSight can connect to Athena for interactive business intelligence dashboards and visualizations.

Data Governance Layer: AWS Lake Formation provides centralized data governance with fine-grained access control at the database, table, column, and row level. Lake Formation simplifies the setup and management of a secure data lake by providing a central console to define and enforce data access policies. Lake Formation integrates with the Glue Data Catalog to manage permissions on cataloged tables and databases. It supports tag-based access control (TBAC) for scalable permission management across hundreds of tables and thousands of users. Lake Formation also provides data sharing capabilities across AWS accounts and AWS Organizations, enabling secure cross-account data collaboration without copying data.

Orchestration and Metadata Layer: Amazon DynamoDB stores pipeline metadata, job execution status, data lineage information, and configuration parameters for the orchestration layer. DynamoDB's single-digit millisecond latency enables real-time pipeline status dashboards and rapid lookup of processing history.

Monitoring and Security: Amazon CloudWatch provides end-to-end monitoring and logging across all data lake components. CloudWatch Metrics tracks Glue job durations, Lambda invocations and errors, S3 storage metrics, and Athena query performance. CloudWatch Logs captures execution logs from Lambda functions and Glue jobs. CloudWatch Alarms notify operators via Amazon SNS when pipeline failures, data quality violations, or cost anomalies occur. AWS CloudTrail records all API calls across the data lake for audit logging, security analysis, and compliance. AWS IAM policies and Lake Formation permissions enforce least-privilege access boundaries across the entire data lake. S3 access logging tracks all requests to data lake buckets. VPC endpoints enable private connectivity between services without traversing the public internet.

The end-to-end data flow is as follows: Source systems deposit raw data files into the S3 raw zone. S3 Event Notifications trigger EventBridge, which routes events through content-based rules to the appropriate processing pipeline. For simple transformations, Lambda functions validate and preprocess data directly. For complex ETL workflows, Step Functions orchestrate multi-step pipelines that invoke Glue crawlers to update schemas, run Glue ETL jobs to transform data from raw to processed to curated zones, and update DynamoDB pipeline metadata at each stage. Processed data in S3 is cataloged in the Glue Data Catalog and governed by Lake Formation. Business analysts and data scientists query curated data using Athena SQL queries or connect via QuickSight for dashboards. All operations are logged in CloudWatch and CloudTrail for operational visibility and compliance auditing.
